title: The ever-elusive phylogenetic history of forest tree populations and species. A commentary on: ‘Postglacial genetic legacies and climate-driven demography inform conservation of silver fir’
content: Discovering the genetic diversity of populations and understanding their clustering according to their ancestry and phylogenetic origin has become a central goal in conservation science and practice. The assessment of genetic diversity is an essential tool for designing conservation strategies, both for locating meaningful populations and avoiding gaps in situ, and prioritizing populations that deserve relocation in ex situ conservation sites (Fady and Scotti-Saintagne, 2025). It is also a recognized target of conservation by the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity.
